last.verdict: MetLife posted its best-ever quarterly profit per share, but a big part came from volatile investment gains rather than steadier insurance growth.

takeaways.label: Record, but investment-aided
takeaways.text: Adjusted EPS excluding one-time items hit a record $2.85, up 22%. Gains from private-equity-type investments jumped 49% to $720 million, a swingy source.

takeaways.label: Broad underlying growth
takeaways.text: Core revenue excluding pension risk transfers rose 8% to $13.5 billion, growing in all six segments. Group Benefits earnings rose 15% on favorable claims.

takeaways.label: Latin America and Asia softer
takeaways.text: Latin America earnings excluding one-time items fell 5% at constant currency on lower investment returns. Asia sales fell 6% against a strong prior year.

takeaways.label: Annual review dented headline
takeaways.text: The yearly review of insurance assumptions cut adjusted earnings by $46 million, pulling retirement-unit earnings down 6%. Excluding it, that unit rose 12%.

history.verdict: Investors cheered a clear profit beat driven by better insurance claims results.

reasons.label: Earnings beat
reasons.text: Adjusted earnings of $2.43 per share topped analyst estimates of about $2.29.

reasons.label: Better claims results
reasons.text: Group Benefits profit jumped 25% to $503 million on favorable underwriting and volume growth.

reasons.label: Broad growth, high returns
reasons.text: Every segment grew; return on equity hit 17% for a second straight quarter.
